source_text: Hinc potius suos approbat, quod ante proprium voluntatis obsequium, hoc quod in eis fecit beneficiorum sublimat augmentis In una igitur eademque causa, alius relinquitur iustitia iudicante, non fato; alius assumitur gratia praestante, non merito
pass_a_gloss: From-here rather his-own approbat, that/which before proprium of-will obsequium, this that/which in to-them made beneficiorum raises-up augmentis in together therefore the-same-and case/cause, other leaves justice iudicante, not fato; other assumitur grace praestante, not deservedly.

lemmas.lexica: LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'
LS meritum=desert; Blaise without later merit-system

pass_b_english: The grace of Christ’s mysteries is rich in many gifts.
Rather, he shows them to be his own by raising what he made in them through additional benefits, before their own obedient exercise of will.

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: In the suum cuique definition gratia is partiality, not saving grace.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
